subject: stat_bin() / coord_polar() --> create a wind rose

messages.author: 06184d21891cb6ea
messages.subject: stat_bin() / coord_polar() --> create a wind rose
parts:
Hi all,

I would like to produce a wind rose using stat_bin() and coord_polar() from ggplot2 package. This is almost done except one thing: I would like to center the display of each bin (binwidth: 15°) on the center of each wind sector for a better visualization. For that purpose, I’ve adjusted the “origin” argument to -7.5 explained in “R Graphics Cookbook” Chapter 8, recipe 8.16 page 199 – 200 :”We’ll set binwidth to 15 and make the origin of the histogram start at -7.5, so each bin is centered around 0, 15 ,30, etc..”. This is what I want, but in the end, it doesn’t work as I expected it to. Actually, a bin is lost and the North sector bin is not displayed in the wind rose.

In the histogram, occurences for the North sector (bins -7.5 - 7.5 and 352.5 - 367.5) are plotted but not in the wind rose, they aren’t. Is it because I'm dealing with polar plot and overlapping data? This is my feeling when I see that, in the temporary data frame produced by stat_bin(), -7.5 and 367.5 are replaced by NA.

Eventually, what I need is the sum of the counts of both bins 352.5 – 360 and 0 – 7.5.  As one can see, these data are in the tmp df but they are, unfortunately, not used…

 What is the best way to achieve what I want to do or what can I do to handle this situation ?

Is it possible to modify the tmp data frame by myself and then use it to carry out the plot ?

Here below, you will find the code that I use, whereas the data are in the attached csv file.

Many thanks in advance for answers!

Laurent

 

library(ggplot2)

 

data<-read.csv(file = "dataLSP.csv")

data$cat<-""

z<-which(data$ws>0 & data$ws<=0.001)

a<-which(data$ws>0.001 & data$ws<=2)

b<-which(data$ws>2 & data$ws<=4)

c<-which(data$ws>4 & data$ws<=6)

d<-which(data$ws>6 & data$ws<=10)

 

data$cat[a]<-"]1-2]"

data$cat[b]<-"]2-4]"

data$cat[c]<-"]4-6]"

data$cat[d]<-"]6-10]"

 

 

hist<-ggplot(data = data,mapping = aes(x=wd,fill=cat))+

  stat_bin(binwidth=15,origin=-7.5, colour="black",size=.25,position="stack")+

  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0,360,15))

 

x<-print(hist)

head(x[["data"]][[1]],n=8)

tail(x[["data"]][[1]],n=8) 


 

wr<-ggplot(data = data,mapping = aes(x=wd,fill=cat))+

  stat_bin(binwidth=15,origin=-7.5, colour="black",size=.25)+

  coord_polar()+

  scale_fill_brewer(guide=guide_legend(reverse=T))+

  scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,360),breaks=seq(0,360,by=45),minor_breaks=seq(0,360,by=15),labels=c("N","NE","E","SE","S","SO","O","NO",""))

 

y<-print(wr)

head(y[["data"]][[1]], n=8)

tail(y[["data"]][[1]], n=8)
